items.title: A monic polynomial over a ring is divisible by T minus each of its roots
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the first structural fact used in the section on descent of flatness along integral maps: a monic polynomial P over an arbitrary ring with a root alpha factors as (T - alpha) times a monic Q (statement lines 4551-4555). The author's proof is an 8-line induction on the degree which uses polynomial division by the monic linear factor T - alpha and evaluates the remainder at alpha (proof lines 4558-4565). What a reader has to supply is that division with remainder by a monic polynomial is available over an arbitrary ring, including over a ring with zero divisors, and that evaluating (T - alpha)Q + r at alpha leaves exactly r: the two steps are standard but they are what makes the argument work and the author does not spell them out beyond recording the division. Everything else in the proof is the induction, which is carried out for all degrees including the case where the ring is not a domain.
